ending_first.ending: The story ends with Neo fully become 'the One.' After Agent Smith shoots him three times in a hotel hallway and the crew gives him up for dead, Trinity refuses to let him go and calls him back to life. Neo opens his eyes, raises a hand to stop the Agents' bullets in midair, and suddenly sees the simulation as raw code he can rewrite. He steps inside Agent Smith and bursts out of him, destroying the program—an act so impossible that the remaining Agents feel fear for the first time. In the real world, just as machines breach the ship, Neo dives through a ringing phone to safety and, aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, wakes beside Trinity. He re-enters the Matrix only to make a public declaration: he will show the enslaved a world without rules, without Agents, without limits, and set them free. Then he hangs up and flies above the city skyline.

s01_in_the_cracks_of_a_wrong_world.text: In a late-1990s-seeming city, two lives run in parallel. By day Thomas A. Anderson is an ordinary software employee who is chewed out for lateness and told to toe the line. By night, as the hacker 'Neo,' he senses that something is deeply wrong with the world—a splinter in the mind he can't name. When a message types itself onto his own screen and tells him to 'follow the white rabbit,' he obeys a pull he doesn't understand, and meets a legendary hacker called Trinity, who knows him by a name he's never spoken aloud. She tells him the answer to his lifelong question—'What is the Matrix?'—is out there waiting, if he's brave enough to find it.

s02_pulled_out_of_the_ordinary.text: Neo is hunted in his own workplace. Guided only by a voice over a phone, he narrowly slips past armed intruders but is cornered and, refusing to name the man he's come to trust, is captured. His captor, the cold program Agent Smith, lays bare Neo's double life and offers to erase it in exchange for a betrayal; when Neo refuses, his mouth is sealed shut and a mechanical tracker is burrowed into his flesh. He is woken by a ringing phone, led into the rain, and brought before Morpheus—the man whose name he protected. Morpheus offers him a choice that cannot be undone: a blue pill that lets him forget and wake up believing whatever he wants, or a red pill that shows him 'how deep the rabbit hole goes.' Neo takes the red pill.

s03_the_desert_of_the_real.text: Neo wakes in the real world for the first time—his body atrophied, his head shaved, ejected from a fluid-filled pod in a vast field of identical pods holding unconscious human beings. He is pulled aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, a battered hovercraft, where his unused muscles are rebuilt and the truth is forced on him: the world he knew is the Matrix, a shared dream fed to human minds while machines farm their bodies for power. The sky was scorched long ago; what's left of free humanity clings to the last city, Zion. Neo recoils at the horror of it. Morpheus, certain Neo is someone more, begins to train him.

s04_learning_that_the_mind_is_the_weapon.text: Inside the Matrix, Morpheus teaches Neo that the rules of the simulated world can be bent—but only by a mind that truly believes. Neo downloads fighting skills in hours yet is still thrown to the floor, because knowing the path and walking it are not the same. He fails a leap between rooftops because, deep down, he doesn't believe he can make it. All the while Morpheus speaks of an old prophecy: that a chosen 'One' would rise and free humanity. Neo cannot believe this is about him. Only Trinity seems to see something in him worth betting on, and her quiet faith unsettles them both.

s05_the_verdict_and_the_betrayal.text: Morpheus takes Neo to the Oracle, a seer who lives hidden among the powerless. She gives Neo a private verdict that deepens his doubt, and a warning Morpheus must never repeat. But the trip is a trap. A crewmate, Cypher—sick of the hardship of freedom and hungry for the easy pleasures of the simulation—has secretly struck a deal with Agent Smith: he will hand over Morpheus in exchange for being plugged back into the Matrix to live a comfortable lie. As the Agents close in, Cypher murders two of his own crew and delivers Morpheus into captivity, only to be stopped by a wounded crewmate who survived. The remaining few escape, but Morpheus is taken.

s06_the_choice_to_believe.text: Morpheus is tortured for the access codes to humanity's last city, and the crew prepares to abandon him rather than let the machines in. But Neo stops them. He still doesn't believe he is the One—so his decision to go back isn't about a prophecy. It's a wager on the man who believed in him. With Trinity at his side, Neo storms the building where Morpheus is held, and this time he doesn't fall short: he moves with a certainty he's never had, pulls Morpheus out under a hail of gunfire, and fights his way to an exit. On the run afterward, he is cornered in a subway station, alone with Agent Smith. Beaten to the edge of death, Neo refuses the fate Smith pronounces over him—and for the first time, something in him breaks open and he escapes.

s07_death_and_the_one_awakened.text: Chased to a dead-end hotel hallway, Neo is shot three times and dies in Trinity's arms while machines close in on the ship in the real world. Trinity will not accept it. She tells him what the Oracle once told her—that she would fall in love with the One, and that meant he could not truly die—and calls him back with a kiss. Neo's heart restarts. He rises, and now he sees the Matrix for what it is: flowing code he can reach out and rewrite. He halts the Agents' bullets with a raised hand, then steps inside Agent Smith and destroys him, so that the surviving programs feel fear for the first time. He escapes through a ringing phone just as the ship is overrun. Waking beside Trinity, Neo re-enters the world he can now reshape and promises the enslaved that he will show them anything they want—a world without rules—and then flies above the city.

jacket_copy:
Thomas Anderson lives two lives: a quiet office drone by day, a hunted hacker named Neo by night, forever haunted by a single question he can't stop asking—what is the Matrix? When a mysterious rebel named Trinity and the legendary Morpheus offer him the truth, Neo takes a choice that cannot be undone. He wakes into a scorched, machine-ruled reality where the world he knew was only a dream fed to keep humanity docile, and where the mind itself is the only weapon that matters.

Told he is the fulfillment of an ancient prophecy, Neo cannot believe it—and every brutal test proves him right. Trained to bend the rules of a simulated world, he still falls short, still doubts, still fears he is nothing special.
